nodes.content: Develop a learned large-eddy closure reconciling local energy backscatter with long-horizon stability across unseen Reynolds numbers.
requirements: Reduce kinetic-energy spectrum error by 20% versus dynamic Smagorinsky on held-out Reynolds numbers.
Maintain bounded kinetic energy for 100 eddy-turnover times without suppressing all local backscatter.

nodes.content: Train a Galilean-invariant neural SGS stress with spectrum and rollout losses, plus energy-dependent net-dissipation projection preserving local backscatter.
Can the net-dissipation projection bound kinetic energy for 100 eddy-turnover times at unseen Reynolds numbers while retaining local backscatter?
Enforcing net SGS dissipation ≥ forcing power above 1.5× training-set mean energy bounds 100-turnover energy while preserving local backscatter.
Train projected/unprojected closures at Reλ=80,120; test Reλ=160,200 over 100 turnovers, comparing energy maxima, backscatter frequency, and spectral error.
Run 100-turnover LES at Reλ=160,200 with projected and unprojected closures; measure energy exceedances, local backscatter frequency, and spectral error.
At Reλ=160,200, projected energy stayed below 1.5× training mean for 100 turnovers; 12% of cells backscattered.
Ablate the 1.5× energy trigger and forcing-power dissipation floor at Reλ=160,200; compare 100-turnover energy peaks and backscatter fractions.
At Reλ=200, projected backscatter fell to 0% during the final 30 turnovers; removing the floor retained 15%.
Restricting dissipation corrections to forward-transfer cells should sustain ≥10% backscatter while keeping energy ≤1.5× training mean for 100 turnovers.
Implement forward-transfer-only projection; rerun Reλ=160,200 for 100 turnovers, tracking energy, backscatter frequency, and spectra versus dynamic Smagorinsky.
Implement forward-transfer-only projection; run Reλ=160,200 LES for 100 turnovers, logging peak energy, backscatter fraction, and Smagorinsky-relative spectral error.
At Reλ=160,200, 100-turnover peak energy stayed ≤1.47× training mean, backscatter ≥11%, and log-spectrum RMSE fell 25% versus dynamic Smagorinsky.
Stress-test forward-transfer-only projection across five forcing seeds at Reλ=200, recording 100-turnover peak energy and minimum 10-turnover backscatter fraction.
At Reλ=200, forcing seed 4 reached 1.68× training-mean energy by turnover 86, despite 12% backscatter.
Keep forward-transfer-only projection as a candidate for its 25% spectral gain, but defer acceptance after seed-4's 1.68× energy excursion.
Train a neural SGS stress that budgets local backscatter using stored dissipation credits and adapts payouts to forcing.
Can dissipation-credit accounting prevent seed-dependent energy excursions without throttling backscatter enough to erase spectral gains at held-out Reynolds numbers?
A 5-turnover dissipation-credit window with forcing-adjusted payouts will cap energy at 1.5× training mean while preserving ≥10% backscatter.
Test five-turnover credit closure across five Reλ=160,200 seeds for 100 turnovers; measure peak energy, backscatter, Smagorinsky-relative spectral RMSE.
Implement forcing-adjusted, five-turnover credit payouts; run five Reλ=160,200 seeds for 100 turnovers, recording energy peaks, backscatter, spectral RMSE.
Across five Reλ=160,200 seeds over 100 turnovers: peak energy ≤1.42× training mean; backscatter ≥11%; spectral RMSE 23% below dynamic Smagorinsky.
CreditLES-v1 release: trained SGS weights, five-turnover credit ledger implementation, Reλ=160/200 rollout logs, and spectral-RMSE evaluation scripts.
Adopt CreditLES-v1, with released weights and scripts, for 23% lower spectral RMSE, bounded 100-turnover energy, and ≥11% backscatter.
Train a shell-conditioned, globally energy-neutral SGS transfer stress atop positive eddy viscosity to permit local backscatter without net injection.
Can energy-neutral shell transfers correct inertial-range spectral bias at held-out Reynolds numbers while retaining local backscatter?
Train energy-neutral shell transfers at Reλ=80,120; evaluate 100-turnover Reλ=160,200 spectra, energy, backscatter against dynamic Smagorinsky and CreditLES-v1.
Train energy-neutral shell-transfer stress at Reλ=80,120; run 100-turnover Reλ=160,200 LES, measuring spectral RMSE, energy peaks, and backscatter.
At Reλ=160,200, shell transfers reduced log-spectrum RMSE only 9% versus dynamic Smagorinsky, despite 11% local backscatter.
Compute shell-resolved SGS flux and spectral-error contributions at Reλ=160,200 versus filtered DNS and CreditLES-v1.
At Reλ=160,200, inertial-shell log-spectrum RMSE fell 24% versus dynamic Smagorinsky; near-cutoff errors limited the overall gain.
Defer shell-transfer closure as standalone: 24% inertial-shell improvement cannot offset near-cutoff errors, leaving only 9% overall spectral gain.
Augment CreditLES-v1 with energy-neutral inertial-shell transfers while retaining its dissipation-credit ledger to control long-horizon energy.
Do inertial-shell transfers improve CreditLES-v1 spectral RMSE without disrupting its credit ledger or reducing local backscatter?
Adding energy-neutral inertial-shell transfers to CreditLES-v1 reduces held-out spectral RMSE ≥5% while preserving ≤1.5× energy and ≥10% backscatter.
Integrate shell transfers into CreditLES-v1; compare five-seed Reλ=160,200 100-turnover spectra, peak energy, and backscatter against unmodified CreditLES-v1.
Run five-seed Reλ=160,200 100-turnover LES with shell-augmented CreditLES-v1; compare spectral RMSE, peak energy, backscatter to baseline.
Across five Reλ=160,200 seeds, shell augmentation lowered log-spectrum RMSE 7% versus CreditLES-v1; 100-turnover peak energy was 1.44× mean, backscatter ≥11%.
CreditLES-Shell-v2 package: augmented weights, energy-neutral shell-transfer module, five-seed Reλ=160/200 rollouts, and spectral-RMSE comparison scripts.
Reproduce CreditLES-Shell-v2 package rollouts at Reλ=160,200; audit 100-turnover shell neutrality, ledger balance, backscatter, and CreditLES-v1-relative spectral RMSE.
Reλ=160,200 replay confirmed neutral transfers, nonnegative credits, ≤1.44× peak energy, ≥11% backscatter, and 7% lower RMSE versus CreditLES-v1.
Under abrupt forcing changes, can CreditLES-Shell-v2 preserve nonnegative credits and bounded energy without losing local backscatter?
At Reλ=200, double forcing for turnovers 40–50 across five seeds; track 100-turnover peak energy, minimum credits, and backscatter.
Run packaged CreditLES-Shell-v2 across five Reλ=200 seeds, doubling forcing during turnovers 40–50; log 100-turnover energy peaks, credit minima, backscatter.
Under doubled forcing, Reλ=200 seed 3 peaked at 1.73× training-mean energy; credits hit zero despite 11% backscatter.
Re-run depleted-credit Reλ=200 seed 3 with both closures under doubled forcing; compare spectral RMSE, peak energy, and backscatter.
Before the forcing pulse, seed 3 showed 7% lower spectral RMSE versus CreditLES-v1, ≤1.44× energy, and 11% backscatter.
Conditionally adopt CreditLES-Shell-v2 for steady forcing after replicated 7% spectral gains and 11% backscatter; defer pulse deployment after 1.73× excursion.
Select CreditLES-v1 for tested steady forcing; conditionally use Shell-v2 there, shelving standalone shells and seed-unstable projection.
